Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Travel & transport

cancel verb

an arrangement or a booking

also call off, cancellation, be cancelled, cancelled

classical

Plaut. Stich. 4.2.19: jubē domī cēnam coquī atque ad illum renūntiārī (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Verr. 2.2.89: hospitium eī renūntiat

renūntiō, renūntiāre, renūntiāvī, renūntiātum

verb, first conjugation

send word that it is off: cancel

Lewis & Short: to retract, revoke, give up, renounce. Of a dinner one has accepted, to send word that one will not come (Plautus); of a friendship or an agreement, to call it off (Cicero, Livy).

Other words

  • omittō, omittere, omīsī, omissum — give up, drop (a plan)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical

    Lewis & Short: to lay aside, give up. For a plan one simply drops.

  • abrogō, abrogāre, abrogāvī, abrogātum — repeal (a law)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · M-O s.v. cancel

    Classically to repeal a law or take away an office (Lewis & Short): for what an authority cancels, not for a dinner.

Examples

  • Avia cēnam renūntiāvit; aegrōtat.

    Grandma has called off dinner; she’s ill.composed

See also book, meeting.

SourcesLewis & Short: renuntio · Lewis & Short: omitto · Lewis & Short: abrogo

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. cancel.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
